subject: Recap: FinSecure - Deployment mode & data isolation requirements
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@finsecure.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finsecure.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: FinSecure - Deployment mode & data isolation requirements

Hi Alex / Priya

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the next steps we discussed. If I captured anything incorrectly, please flag it and I'll update.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Primary requirement: strict data isolation. FinSecure needs assurance that customer data never leaves their environment or is accessible to any multi-tenant compute.
- Deployment preference: leaning toward Private VPC or on-prem (air-gapped) for initial rollout; Dedicated was discussed as a possible intermediate if Private VPC proves too heavy operationally.
- Encryption & keys: you require customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and in-transit + at-rest encryption with no readability by Redwood personnel.
- Audit & evidence: you asked for SOC 2 report, network architecture diagram, and audit log retention details.

Next steps we agreed:
1) I'll attach the SOC 2 report and our deployment summary (attached).
2) Marissa will follow up with a short technical note on how we implement VPC peering, private endpoints, and egress controls.
3) Dev (cc'd) will answer two security-specific questions you raised (HSM support & audit log retention).
4) We'll schedule a technical deep-dive next week to map your network requirements vs our Private VPC/on-prem options.

Questions we still have from our side (so we can scope any Private/on-prem work):
- Do you require physical air-gap (no internet) for the initial phase, or is a Private VPC with strict egress controls acceptable?
- Any regulatory timelines we should know about? (PCI/GLBA deadlines, audits in next 6 months)

Attachments: SOC2-report-2025.pdf; redwood-deployment-summary.pdf

Thanks
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.inference

From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@finsecure.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finsecure.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: FinSecure - Deployment mode & data isolation requirements

Rachel

Thanks for the clear recap. That matches our notes. Quick clarifications:
- For phase 1 we prefer Private VPC with strict no-egress policies; air-gap would be ideal but could be delayed to phase 2 depending on cost/ops.
- Customer-managed KMS is required, and keys must be rotated under our policies.
- Audit logs must be retained for a minimum of 7 years for compliance and be exportable to our SIEM.

We're happy to do the technical deep-dive next Tuesday morning PT. Priya can you confirm availability?

Best,
Alex
Director of IT Security, FinSecure
alex.torres@finsecure.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@finsecure.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.inference>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: FinSecure - Deployment mode & data isolation requirements

Alex / Rachel

Following up with a short technical note (high level) on how Redwood supports Private VPC and Dedicated capacity with respect to data isolation:

Private VPC (our recommended path for strict isolation):
- Customer VPC peering or PrivateLink style private endpoints; all inference traffic flows over the customer network.
- No egress to the public internet from the inference nodes; egress gateways can be disabled.
- Customer-managed KMS integration: we support bringing your own keys via KMS/HSM. Keys are only used within the enclave and are never exported.
- Audit logs: we stream request/response metadata (token-level cost, timestamps, model id) to customers' secure log sinks (S3/GCS with encryption) and can retain per your policy 7+ years supported via long-term storage.
- On-prem option: full air-gapped deployment is supported for enterprise engagements; this is a professional-services-led project (network changes + installation).

Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools):
- Runs in our managed environment; provides tenant isolation at the compute level but shares control plane systems.
- For customers with less stringent regulatory needs, Dedicated provides predictable throughput and simpler onboarding.

Action items from our side:
- I'll attach a short network-requirements checklist for Tuesday's deep-dive. (See attached network-requirements-finsecure.xlsx)
- Dev, can you confirm HSM integration and exact audit log fields we can stream?

Happy to go deeper on Tuesday.

Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: network-requirements-finsecure.xlsx]

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@finsecure.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: FinSecure - Deployment mode & data isolation requirements

Alex

Quick answers to the security-specific items you asked about:

1) HSM / KMS: we support BYOK via AWS KMS and customer-controlled HSMs. Keys are used in a way that prevents Redwood operators from extracting plaintext. For on-prem deployments we support local HSM appliances and FIPS-compliant modules.

2) Audit log fields: we can stream the following minimum set to your SIEM/bucket: timestamp, request id, model id, route, token_count (no token contents), response hash, caller tenant id, processing latency, error codes. We do not include request/response plaintext by default unless you opt-in for debug capture; debug capture can be disabled for production.

3) Retention: we can configure long-term retention to meet your 7-year requirement; we'll estimate S3/GCS costs as part of the next proposal.

I'll join Tuesday's session to go through network ports, peering, and the HSM flow.

Dev
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: none]
